title: eRNA and eDNA Co-Extraction from Water Samples Using NucleoMag Kit
author: Marine Vautier
materials: In this step, the buffers provided by the kit are distributed in a plate. For RNA extraction from filtered water samples, the 12 columns of the plate are divided into 2 sections of 6 columns each, allowing up to 16 samples to be extracted per plate. Annotate the plate as recommended below: Table 1: Recommended eRNA plaque annotation Note: It is useful to mark the dividing line between columns 6 and 7 with a marker pen to provide a visual cue for filling the plate. Add the appropriate buffers into the appropriate wells of the plate (Table 2): 1 st column / 7 th column: Will be filled during plate preparation 2/2 2 nd column / 8 th column: 850 µL of MWA3 (1 st wash) 3 rd column / 9 th column: 850 µL of MWA3 (2 nd wash) 4 th column /10 th column: Will be filled during plate preparation 2/2 5 th column / 11 th column: 850 µL of MWA4 (3 rd wash and bead drying) Note: The choice of elution volume is based on the expected eRNA amount. In this step, the buffers provided by the kit are distributed in a plate. For DNA extraction from filtered water samples, the 12 columns of the plate are divided into 2 sections of 6 columns each, allowing up to 16 samples to be extracted per plate.

steps.title: Aliquot buffers and label tubes
steps.instruction: Aliquot kit buffers to avoid contamination: put MWA1, MWA2, MWA3 and MWA4 into 50 mL tubes; put NucleoMag B‑Beads solution and RNase‑free H₂O into 2 mL tubes. Annotate tubes as follows – one 2 mL tube per sample for lysate collection, two 5 mL tubes per 8 samples for the NucleoMag B‑Beads + MWA2 mix, and two 1.5 mL tubes per sample for RNA and DNA collection.

steps.title: Decontaminate scissors
steps.instruction: Before starting and between each filter cutting, wash scissors with RNase‑off/DNase‑off solution, rinse with ethanol, then dip sequentially into three 50 mL tubes containing (1) 10 % H₂O₂, (2) molecular‑biology‑grade water, and (3) ethanol, opening and closing the scissors in each tube.

steps.title: Prepare rDNase solution
steps.instruction: Reconstitute lyophilized rDNase by adding 4 mL reaction buffer, incubate 2–3 min at room temperature, and gently shake to dissolve (avoid vigorous agitation). Transfer to a 50 mL tube, add 28 mL reaction buffer, gently shake. The 32 mL solution suffices for 96 samples; aliquot if fewer samples are processed, store aliquots at –20 °C (no more than three freeze‑thaw cycles) and place one aliquot in the fridge a few hours before use.

steps.title: Lysis of pre‑buffered samples
steps.instruction: Collect the 5 mL tubes that contain the filters. If frozen, defrost 10 min at room temperature. Cut the filter into small pieces directly in the tube using decontaminated scissors (decontaminate between samples). Vortex vertically for 5 min at maximum speed, then place tubes in a benchtop centrifuge. Pipette the lysate into a labeled 2 mL tube, centrifuge at 11 000 rpm (or 11 000 × g) for 30 s at room temperature, and keep the tubes at room temperature until distribution to the plate.

steps.title: Lysis of unbuffered samples
steps.instruction: Collect the 5 mL tubes with filters from the freezer and keep on ice. Immediately add 1 100 µL MWA1 buffer to each tube. Cut the filter into small pieces with decontaminated scissors (decontaminate between samples). Vortex vertically for 5 s at median speed, then horizontally for 5 min at maximum speed. Transfer tubes to a benchtop centrifuge, pipette ~900 µL lysate into a labeled 2 mL tube, centrifuge at 11 000 × g for 30 s at room temperature, and keep at room temperature until plate distribution.

steps.title: Prepare beads‑MWA2 mix (general)
steps.instruction: For each set of up to 8 samples, prepare two 5 mL tubes (one for the RNA plate, one for the DNA plate). Add only MWA2 buffer to each tube; the NucleoMag B‑Beads will be added later. Vortex the NucleoMag B‑Beads tube vigorously, then add the volume of beads specified for the number of samples (see Table 3/4), vortex again, and keep the mix homogeneous by vortexing between samples.

steps.title: Set up eRNA plate
steps.instruction: Remove the film from the 96‑well plate. Add the following to each well: – Columns 4/10: 500 µL of the NucleoMag B‑Beads + MWA2 mix and 450 µL of lysate (supernatant from the 2 mL tubes). – Columns 6/12: 50 µL or 65 µL RNase‑free H₂O (RNA elution). – Columns 1/7: 300 µL rDNase mix (slowly agitate the rDNase tube before dispensing). Film the plate again and proceed immediately to the next step.

steps.title: RNA extraction – part 1
steps.instruction: Place the eRNA plate into the MagnetaPure 32 System, insert the magnetic‑rod cover, select the program for RNA extraction part 1 (Table 5), and start the run (≈35 min).

steps.title: Add MWA2 post‑digestion
steps.instruction: When the DNA digestion step finishes, remove the plate and add 350 µL MWA2 buffer to each well of columns 1 and 7.

steps.title: RNA extraction – part 2
steps.instruction: Place the plate back into the MagnetaPure 32 System (magnetic‑rod cover remains), select the program for RNA extraction part 2 (Table 10), and start the run (≈30 min).

steps.title: Collect and store eRNA
steps.instruction: After the run, remove the plate, place it on ice in the DNA/RNA workstation, remove the magnetic‑rod cover and UV‑decontaminate the instrument. Transfer each eRNA extract into a pre‑annotated 1.5 mL tube (aliquot directly to avoid freeze‑thaw cycles), optionally measure concentration/quality (e.g., Nanodrop), and store extracts at –80 °C.

steps.title: Annotate eDNA plate
steps.instruction: Mark the dividing line between columns 6 and 7 with a pen. Add the following buffers: – Columns 2/8: 850 µL MWA3 (first wash). – Columns 3/9: 850 µL MWA3 (second wash). – Columns 4/10: 850 µL MWA4 (third wash and bead drying). Columns 5/11 are left empty. Columns 1/7 and 6/12 will be filled during plate preparation.

steps.title: Add washes to eDNA plate
steps.instruction: After annotation, film the plate and keep it at room temperature until the next step.

steps.title: Prepare beads‑MWA2 mix for eDNA
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the lysate prepared in step 5 at 11 000 rpm (or × g) for 30 s at room temperature. Vigorously vortex the NucleoMag B‑Beads tube, add the volume of beads required for each MWA2 buffer tube (see Table 3), vortex the mix, and keep it homogeneous.

steps.title: Set up eDNA plate
steps.instruction: Remove the film from the eDNA plate. Add to each well: – Columns 1/7: 500 µL of the NucleoMag B‑Beads + MWA2 mix and 450 µL of lysate (supernatant from the 2 mL tubes). – Columns 6/12: 50 µL or 65 µL DNase‑free H₂O (DNA elution). Film the plate again and keep at room temperature.

steps.title: DNA extraction
steps.instruction: Place the eDNA plate into the MagnetaPure 32 System, insert the magnetic‑rod cover, select the program matching the chosen elution volume and temperature (heating to 56 °C improves yield but may cause evaporation), and start the run (≈40 min).

steps.title: Collect and store eDNA
steps.instruction: When the run ends, remove the plate, place it in the DNA workstation, remove the magnetic‑rod cover and UV‑decontaminate the instrument. Transfer each eDNA extract into a pre‑annotated 1.5 mL tube, optionally measure concentration/quality (e.g., Nanodrop), and store extracts at 4 °C for immediate use or at –20 °C / –80 °C for long‑term storage.
